findings.title: #258/#259 RLS write policies may still be live in production
findings.evidence: PR #258 and #259 are merged. Migration headers and PR titles say the SQL was NOT APPLIED to production. In-repo end-state drops approvals_write_member, audit_insert_member, orgs_update_admin, subscriptions_write_admin and 17 phase-2 write policies, and REVOKE writes from anon/authenticated. A DB created from current schema.sql is fine; an existing prod DB that never ran these files still lets a tenant session JWT + anon key write approvals, plans, credentials, and bindings via PostgREST.
findings.exploitability: High if unapplied (self-approve, forge audit, rewrite plan_key/credentials). None if applied. Cannot be closed from git.
findings.fix: Run NEEDS-VALIDATION.md section A. If policies remain, apply 20261004500000 then 20261004600000 then 20261004800000 in a reviewed window.

findings.title: Global Telegram webhook: unscoped approval lookup + empty allowlist allows any Telegram user
findings.evidence: isAllowedUser returns true when TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS is empty (route.ts:81-85). handleCallback calls getApprovalByTelegramRef(match[2]) without orgId (route.ts:207). getApprovalByTelegramRef only adds .eq('org_id') when orgId is passed (approvals.ts:593-612). telegram_ref is 48 bits (tokens.ts:9-12). Route still requires TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET (route.ts:351-364). Tenant [ref] routes pass channel.orgId.
findings.exploitability: Live only if the global bot webhook is registered, allowlist is empty, and an attacker has or brute-forces a telegram_ref.
findings.fix: Fail closed on empty allowlist. Always pass orgId. Retire global bot per docs/production-cutover.md and multi-tenant audit M1/M2.
findings.flag_dependency: Depends on TELEGRAM_* env (pilot). Not a feature-flags.ts flag.

findings.title: DEMO mode on a public host collapses dashboard authentication
findings.evidence: isDemoMode() is true when any of URL/anon/service_role looks like a placeholder (mode.ts:24-32). getSessionContext then always returns the demo org (session.ts:92-100). requireCapability honors x-member-id / ?as= / body actor (demo-actor.ts:76-78). middleware matcher does not cover /api.
findings.exploitability: Anyone who can reach a host left on replace_me_* keys is effectively owner of the demo org.
findings.fix: GET /api/health must return runtimeMode=production and demo=false on every public hostname. Alert on placeholder keys.

findings.title: Decision-workflow RLS policies reference a non-existent members table
findings.evidence: Policies at lines 176-244 use FROM members m. Repo has org_members only. No GRANT/REVOKE in that migration. No app .from('decision_*') found. P1_DECISION_WORKFLOW_ENABLED defaults OFF.
findings.exploitability: Low today (policy errors fail closed for authenticated). High if a members table is later created or the flag is turned on against PostgREST.
findings.fix: Rewrite policies onto org_members or drop them and REVOKE writes from anon/authenticated. Do not enable P1_DECISION_WORKFLOW_ENABLED until fixed.

findings.title: org_members write policy dropped but table-level writes not REVOKEd
findings.evidence: schema.sql:639-645 drops org_members_write_admin and documents server-only writes. Unlike #258 tables there is no REVOKE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE from anon/authenticated.
findings.exploitability: Today RLS default-deny blocks session writes. A future permissive policy would silently reopen role/capability writes.
findings.fix: Add REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON org_members FROM anon, authenticated.

findings.title: Many server-only tables have RLS ON but neither policies nor explicit REVOKE
findings.evidence: Pattern: ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY + no policies + rely on Supabase default GRANTs (e.g. cross_team_wake_bindings, thread_send_leases, comm_reply_send_fingerprints). Newer tables (oauth_*, mcp_event_*, signup_attempts) do REVOKE ALL.
findings.exploitability: Writes fail while no policy exists. A later CREATE POLICY FOR ALL using (true) or is_org_member would reopen the table without a grant change.
findings.fix: Apply the #258 revoke pattern to every server-only table.

findings.title: getApprovalByTelegramRef / getApprovalByTelegramMessageId take optional orgId
findings.evidence: approvals.ts:593-643 add .eq('org_id') only when orgId is provided. Demo path documented as intentionally unscoped when orgId omitted (lib/data/p0-auth-idor.test.ts). Global Telegram is the known caller that omits it (SP-B-001).
findings.exploitability: Any new caller that omits orgId repeats cross-tenant read/action. Current Slack/LINE/[ref] callers pass channel.orgId.
findings.fix: Make orgId required in production builds or split a scoped helper from a legacy one.

findings.title: Multi-org Auth users are pinned to the first org_members row
findings.evidence: getSessionContext loads one active membership: order('created_at').limit(1) (session.ts:147-158). No org switcher in the codebase.
findings.exploitability: User in Org A and Org B always acts as A. Wrong-tenant actions if they believe they are in B; not a cross-read of B via session IDs.
findings.fix: Explicit org selection cookie/claim, or reject a second membership until supported.

findings.title: Approval statusToken is a cross-tenant bearer
findings.evidence: GET /api/approvals/status requires id+token only (status/route.ts:21-42). getApprovalStatusByToken loads by id via service role then timing-safe hash compare (approvals.ts:181-205). Token is st_ + 24 random bytes (~192 bits, tokens.ts:5-7).
findings.exploitability: Leaked pollUrl reads that ticket (any tenant). Entropy is adequate if URLs are not logged. Intentional design until Partner webhook exists.
findings.fix: Never log poll URLs. Optional org claim in the token. Short TTL.

findings.title: SLACK_APPROVAL_STRICT defaults OFF so Slack buttons need no allowlist or voter binding
findings.evidence: feature-flags.ts:29-42. When OFF, existing Slack approval behavior is preserved (no required allowedUserIds / voter_bindings, no team_id reject).
findings.exploitability: A Slack user who can press the button in a reachable message may approve without a binding, depending on channel config.
findings.fix: Enable SLACK_APPROVAL_STRICT in production after the existing rollout review.

findings.title: ADMIN_APPROVER_POLICY_REQUIRED defaults OFF so admin-class tickets accept any single approver
findings.evidence: feature-flags.ts:12-27. When OFF, W1 behavior is any single approver. When ON, missing admin-class route fails closed.
findings.exploitability: A business-route voter can clear admin-class tickets while the flag is OFF.
findings.fix: Enable ADMIN_APPROVER_POLICY_REQUIRED after confirming each tenant has an admin route.

findings.title: Legacy webhook fetch allows RFC1918/loopback/HTTP while WEBHOOK_HARDENING_ENABLED is OFF
findings.evidence: link-local-guard.ts:7-10 documents that flag-OFF only blocks link-local/metadata; loopback, other private ranges, http, any port, redirects unchanged. 169.254.169.254 is blocked. Wake URL is saved with trim only (bindings.ts:536-538).
findings.exploitability: Tenant admin (or stolen dashboard session) sets callbackUrl/wakeWebhookUrl → server-side POST to internal HTTP.
findings.fix: Set WEBHOOK_HARDENING_ENABLED=1 (docs/runbooks/webhook-hardening-d9-rollout-20261005.md). Validate URLs at save.

findings.title: Signup Layer 2 rate limits from #211 default OFF
findings.evidence: PR #211: SIGNUP_ATTEMPT_LOG_ENABLED, SIGNUP_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED, SIGNUP_DOMAIN_CHECK_ENABLED all default OFF. Layer 2 fail-open on DB errors. Unflagged Turnstile+honeypot remain fail-closed outside DEMO.
findings.exploitability: Turnstile bypass or farmed tokens can create orgs at scale; disposable domains accepted.
findings.fix: Enable the #211 trio after signup_attempts is applied. Consider SIGNUP_RATE_LIMIT_REQUIRED_ENABLED.

findings.title: LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED defaults OFF (credential stuffing relies on Supabase only)
findings.evidence: feature-flags.ts:508-516. login/route.ts:107-138 skips app buckets unless the flag is ON.
findings.exploitability: Password spraying limited only by Supabase Auth / network.
findings.fix: Enable LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED and set IP_HASH_KEY.

findings.title: LP inquiry has no Turnstile or rate limit while LP flags are OFF; mails a fixed ops inbox
findings.evidence: inquiry/route.ts:77-107 only applies rate limits when LP_INQUIRY_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED or (bot protection AND client IP). Both flags default OFF (feature-flags.ts:230-345). Recipient is AI_EMP_INQUIRY_NOTIFY_EMAIL (fixed), not caller-chosen.
findings.exploitability: Unauthenticated flood of ops email / Resend quota. Not an open relay.
findings.fix: Enable LP_INQUIRY_BOT_PROTECTION_ENABLED, LP_INQUIRY_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED, and IP_HASH_KEY.

findings.title: MCP_OAUTH_ORG_ALLOWLIST_REQUIRED=false with an empty list opens OAuth to all orgs
findings.evidence: Allowlist-required defaults true (fail-closed empty list). Explicit false + empty list allows every org. Consent still binds grant to session.orgId.
findings.exploitability: Config mistake expands the OAuth surface. One tenant still cannot consent for another org's employee.
findings.fix: Keep the default true. Deploy check: if OAuth is ON, allowlist must be non-empty.
findings.flag_dependency: MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED default OFF; MCP_OAUTH_ORG_ALLOWLIST_REQUIRED default true

findings.title: LP chat treats user text as untrusted LLM input and can incur OpenAI cost when flags are ON
findings.evidence: chat-prompt.ts documents user/history as untrusted. Production OpenAI calls in lib/ are LP chat. LP_CHAT_ENABLED / LP_CHAT_TOOLS_ENABLED / LP_JOURNEYS_ENABLED default OFF.
findings.exploitability: When flags ON: prompt injection against the LP assistant and token-cost abuse (mitigated by guest CSRF/Turnstile if those are also ON).
findings.fix: Keep chat flags OFF until bot protection and rate limits are ON. Pin model IDs (QUARTERLY-OPS-CHECKLIST Q-10).

findings.title: P0_REPLY_POLICY_ENHANCED defaults OFF so reply recipients are not audience-validated
findings.evidence: feature-flags.ts:121-135. When OFF, existing reply policy is preserved and recipient validation is not enforced.
findings.exploitability: An approved or auto path can send to a destination not on the employee audience, depending on the old policy.
findings.fix: Enable P0_REPLY_POLICY_ENHANCED for tenants that mail or post externally.

findings.title: Slack/LINE/Telegram wake text is untrusted input to the external employee model
findings.evidence: Channel text is forwarded to the external AI employee. In-app LLM is not used for scoring. Mitigations: approvals, secret detector, optional P1_TOPIC_GATED_POSTING_ENABLED (default OFF; when OFF all posts still need approval).
findings.exploitability: Indirect prompt injection against the employee. Staffpass cannot fully contain an external model; this is a product residual.
findings.fix: Keep sensitive tools behind approval. Treat wake payloads as untrusted in instructions. Enable topic gate only with fail-closed semantics understood.
findings.flag_dependency: P1_TOPIC_GATED_POSTING_ENABLED default OFF (OFF = all posts need approval)

findings.title: is_org_member / is_org_admin SECURITY DEFINER use search_path = public only
findings.evidence: Lines 59-90. Later RPCs pin search_path to pg_catalog, public. These helpers are used by remaining SELECT policies.
findings.exploitability: Requires ability to create objects in public that shadow org_members — typically not available to anon/authenticated.
findings.fix: SET search_path = pg_catalog, public and schema-qualify org_members.

findings.title: POST /api/employees/interpret is unauthenticated
findings.evidence: POST handler (lines 12-26) has no session check. 1500-char cap. Secret-shaped input rejected. Deterministic rules engine, no LLM, no tenant data.
findings.exploitability: DoS and policy-schema recon. No data exfil.
findings.fix: Require a session or apply IP rate limits.

findings.title: GET /api/health leaks runtimeMode and Stripe/Resend configured flags
findings.evidence: health/route.ts:11-20 is a documented public cutover probe. gateway/health still returns runtimeMode when logged out (lines 12-22).
findings.exploitability: Recon only.
findings.fix: Accept for cutover or drop stripeConfigured/resendConfigured from the public body.

findings.title: Notification webhook_ref and telegram_ref are 48-bit
findings.evidence: generateTelegramRef uses 6 random bytes (tokens.ts:9-12). Notification webhook_ref is globally unique 12 hex chars. Slack/LINE still require signing secrets after lookup. LINE comm refs are 43 chars.
findings.exploitability: Guessing a ref alone does not forge Slack/LINE. Combined with SP-B-001 the short telegram_ref matters.
findings.fix: Lengthen new refs; monitor 404/401 on webhook paths.

findings.title: oauth-purge cron compares CRON_SECRET with string equality
findings.evidence: oauth-purge/route.ts:18-21 uses authorization !== Bearer ${secret}. Other crons use rejectUnauthorizedCron (SHA-256 + timingSafeEqual, placeholder rejected).
findings.exploitability: Theoretical timing leak of CRON_SECRET on this one route.
findings.fix: Call rejectUnauthorizedCron.

findings.title: Global Telegram webhook secret uses string equality
findings.evidence: route.ts:362 compares x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token with !==.
findings.exploitability: Theoretical timing leak of TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
findings.fix: Hash both sides and timingSafeEqual, same as cron-secret.ts.

findings.title: Login CSRF same-origin check runs only when MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED
findings.evidence: login/route.ts:64-67. Forgot-password and holds always check origin.
findings.exploitability: Cross-site POST login is mostly mitigated by SameSite cookies. Relevant if OAuth consent is later enabled without this guard staying on.
findings.fix: Always require same-origin on POST /api/auth/login.

findings.title: MCP CORS * and unauthenticated initialize return server identity
findings.evidence: corsHeaders sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (employee-http.ts:54-59). initialize returns serverInfo/capabilities without a credential (lines 305-312). OAuth ON can 401 initialize unless legacy unauth initialize stays on.
findings.exploitability: Recon of server card. Tokens are Authorization headers, not cookies.
findings.fix: Document as accepted. Keep tokens out of query strings.

findings.title: Authenticated users without an org can auto-provision a trial org via repair-org
findings.evidence: GET/POST provision a trial org if the session user has no membership (invitees blocked). Intended recovery for orphaned Auth users.
findings.exploitability: A user who can create Auth accounts can mint empty trial orgs (signup Turnstile is the main brake).
findings.fix: Rate-limit repair-org; keep invite guard.

findings.title: Wake/callback URLs are not validated at save time
findings.evidence: updateWakeWebhook trims opts.url and stores it (bindings.ts:536-538). validateCallbackUrl exists for MCP Events transport only.
findings.exploitability: Enables SP-C-001. No extra privilege.
findings.fix: Reject non-https / non-public URLs at save, same rules as validateCallbackUrl.

findings.title: LP bot-protection flag ON without Turnstile keys fail-opens
findings.evidence: inquiry/route.ts:144-146 logs and proceeds if the flag is ON but Turnstile is not configured. Signup guard is fail-closed in the same situation.
findings.exploitability: Misconfiguration removes the CAPTCHA while operators believe it is on.
findings.fix: Fail closed (503) when the flag is ON and keys are missing.

findings.title: Signup returns 409 email_exists (mailbox enumeration)
findings.evidence: signup/route.ts:392-406. feature-flags.ts:1071-1075: AUTH_ENUMERATION_HARDENING_ENABLED does not change this 409 (review option A).
findings.exploitability: Anyone can test whether an email is registered.
findings.fix: Unify conflict with a generic success/redirect if product accepts it (option B).

findings.title: AUTH_ENUMERATION_HARDENING_ENABLED defaults OFF
findings.evidence: feature-flags.ts:1059-1078. When OFF, forgot-password uses consume-before-send quotas (weaker oracle / quota burning).
findings.exploitability: Forgot-password quota burning and slightly stronger mailbox oracle.
findings.fix: Enable AUTH_ENUMERATION_HARDENING_ENABLED.

findings.title: MCP_AUTH_FAILURE_AUDIT_ENABLED defaults OFF so mcp_auth_failures stays empty
findings.evidence: feature-flags.ts:943-949. Table and RPC exist; writes only when the flag is ON.
findings.exploitability: Credential spraying against /api/mcp is not recorded for quarterly review.
findings.fix: Enable MCP_AUTH_FAILURE_AUDIT_ENABLED.

findings.title: Cron routes not listed in vercel.json remain callable with CRON_SECRET
findings.evidence: vercel.json schedules a subset. Extra routes still authenticate with CRON_SECRET (some allow raw header forms).
findings.exploitability: Requires leaked CRON_SECRET. Then global cleanup/backfill can be triggered.
findings.fix: Keep secret rotation (Q-04). Optionally 404 unused cron routes unless an invoke header is present.

findings.title: OAuth grant store revoke/touch/get filter by grant id only
findings.evidence: Store helpers keyed by grant id. Dashboard DELETE goes through revokeEmployeeGrant which checks org. No HTTP route found that skips that check.
findings.exploitability: None on current HTTP paths. A future caller of revokeGrant(id) could revoke the wrong tenant grant.
findings.fix: Add .eq('org_id', orgId) on revoke/touch where the caller knows org.

findings.title: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is not used on any table
findings.evidence: No FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY in migrations or schema.sql. Table owners and service_role bypass RLS (standard Supabase).
findings.exploitability: N/A; documents the trust model. service_role compromise is total.
findings.fix: None required. Protect SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (Q-04).

findings.title: All tenant writes use the service-role client; RLS is defense-in-depth
findings.evidence: createSupabaseAdminClient() is the write path. Tests pin zero user-session writers to tenant tables. Browser/SSR clients are auth + limited SELECTs.
findings.exploitability: N/A. Explains why SP-A-001 matters for PostgREST, not for app routes.
findings.fix: Keep the write-path tests. Apply #258-style revokes so PostgREST matches the app model.

findings.title: POST /api/email and POST /api/trial are removed (404)
findings.evidence: No app/api/email or app/api/trial handlers. Tests at p0-unauth-401.test.ts:165-203 pin 404 and list the only three routes that import mail helpers (signup, LP inquiry, Stripe webhook). Recipients are own-signup, fixed ops inbox, or Stripe customer.
findings.exploitability: None — former open relay is gone. No other route lets callers pick arbitrary To:.
findings.fix: Keep the SEC1 tests.

findings.title: middleware.ts does not match /api/*; each route must self-authenticate
findings.evidence: matcher is /app, /admin, /login, /signup, /onboarding, /lp/ai-employee-corp (middleware.ts:95-97).
findings.exploitability: By design. New /api routes that forget requireOrgSession are unauthenticated.
findings.fix: Keep a CI/lint check that new route.ts files call an auth helper or are in an allowlist (health, webhooks, cron, public LP).

findings.title: No Next.js server actions ('use server') exist
findings.evidence: Repository-wide search for use server returned zero matches. Mutations go through app/api route handlers.
findings.exploitability: None. Smaller CSRF/action ID surface.
findings.fix: None.

findings.title: No production hardcoded API keys or employee badges in app/lib
findings.evidence: sk- / long gb_emp_ literals appear in tests and secret-detector fixtures only.
findings.exploitability: None found.
findings.fix: None.

findings.title: Employee MCP cannot escalate to admin MCP
findings.evidence: resolveAdminCredential returns employee_badge_rejected for gb_emp_ (admin-credential.ts:53-64). Employee tools use cred.orgId. Admin secrets are not returned on employee poll (docs/security-review-20260916.md R3/R8).
findings.exploitability: None as an escalation path.
findings.fix: None.
